section_1.title: The Detective's Dilemma: Introducing Prior Belief
section_1.content: Introduce the core concept of Bayes' Theorem not as a dry formula, but as a method for updating beliefs based on evidence. We start with a 'Prior Probability'—our best guess before seeing new data.
section_1.example: A Forest Ranger finds a rare 'Cerulean Feather'. She wonders: Is the legendary Blue Phoenix nearby? Without the feather, she knows the Phoenix is rare (1% chance). This 1% is her 'Prior Belief' (P(H)).

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Unit Square as the Universal Set
section_2.content: To visualize probability geometrically, we represent the entire 'Universe of Possibilities' as a 1x1 square with an area of 1. Any event is a sub-area within this square.
section_2.example: Draw a square. Split it vertically: a thin sliver (1%) represents 'Phoenix is Present' (H), and the remaining 99% represents 'Phoenix is Absent' (¬H). The total area is 1.0.

section_3.title: The Evidence Filter (Likelihoods)
section_3.content: Introduce 'Likelihoods' as horizontal segments within our vertical strips. We ask: 'If the hypothesis were true, how likely is this evidence?' and 'If it were false, how likely is it?'
section_3.example: Within the 'Phoenix' strip, color 90% of the height to represent 'Likelihood of finding a feather if Phoenix exists' (P(E|H)). In the 'No Phoenix' strip, color a tiny 5% height for 'finding a feather by fluke' (P(E|¬H)).

section_4.title: The Geometry of the Intersection
section_4.content: Focus on the physical overlap. The 'Evidence' (E) has occurred, so everything outside the shaded 'Evidence' area is now impossible. We highlight the intersection of 'Hypothesis' and 'Evidence'.
section_4.example: The screen fades out the unshaded areas. We are left with two rectangles: A (Phoenix + Feather) and B (No Phoenix + Feather). The total area of these two rectangles is the 'Total Probability of Evidence' P(E).

section_5.title: Updating the Belief: The Posterior
section_5.content: Explain that the new probability is simply the ratio of the 'Success' rectangle to the 'Total Evidence' area. This is 'Normalizing' our world to the new evidence.
section_5.example: Zoom into the rectangles from Section 4. The updated belief (Posterior) is: Area(Phoenix + Feather) divided by [Area(Phoenix + Feather) + Area(Fluke Feather)]. Geometrically, it's the proportion of the 'Evidence Strip' that belongs to our Hypothesis.

section_6.title: Mapping Geometry to the Formula
section_6.content: Overlay the standard mathematical notation of Bayes' Theorem onto the geometric shapes created in the previous steps to solidify the connection.
section_6.example: Show P(H|E) = [P(H) * P(E|H)] / P(E). The numerator is the Area of the 'Target Rectangle'; the denominator is the 'Total Shaded Area'. Use color-coded labels to link the variables to the square's dimensions.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Detective's Dilemma: Introducing Prior Belief",
            [
                "Bayes' Theorem helps us update beliefs using new evidence.",
                "We begin with a Prior Belief before seeing data.",
                "Imagine a Ranger seeking a rare Blue Phoenix."
            ]
        )
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_FEATHER = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_RANGER = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_PRIOR = "#ADD8E6"
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a blue feather icon (#00FFFF) and a ranger silhouette (#FFFFFF) on the right grid.
        # Using simple shapes as no assets provided.
        feather = Star(n=5, color=COLOR_FEATHER, fill_opacity=0.8).scale(0.3)
        feather_label = Text("Feather", font_size=16, color=COLOR_FEATHER)
        self.place_at_grid(feather, "B4")
        feather_label.next_to(feather, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        ranger = Square(side_length=0.6, color=COLOR_RANGER, fill_opacity=0.5)
        # Add a "head" to the square to make it look slightly more like a silhouette
        ranger_head = Circle(radius=0.15, color=COLOR_RANGER, fill_opacity=0.8)
        ranger_head.next_to(ranger, UP, buff=0)
        ranger_sil = VGroup(ranger, ranger_head)
        ranger_label = Text("Ranger", font_size=16, color=COLOR_RANGER)
        self.place_at_grid(ranger_sil, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        ranger_label.next_to(ranger_sil, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(feather), FadeIn(feather_label),
            FadeIn(ranger_sil), FadeIn(ranger_label),
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_PRIOR)
        )
        
        prior_eq = MathTex("P(H) = ", color=COLOR_PRIOR, font_size=36)
        prior_val = MathTex("1\\%", color=COLOR_PRIOR, font_size=36)
        prior_group = VGroup(prior_eq, prior_val).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(prior_group, "D3")
        
        prior_label = Text("Prior Belief", font_size=20, color=COLOR_PRIOR)
        prior_label.next_to(prior_group, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(
            Write(prior_group),
            Write(prior_label)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Scale the '1%' text up and down to emphasize our starting guess.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        
        self.play(
            prior_val.animate.scale(1.5),
            run_time=0.6,
            rate_func=there_and_back

        self.wait(3)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        title_text = "The Evidence Filter (Likelihoods)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Likelihoods describe how evidence appears under each scenario.",
            "If the Phoenix is present, finding a feather is likely.",
            "We shade a tall region within the Phoenix strip.",
            "If absent, finding a feather is just a fluke.",
            "We shade a tiny region in the non-Phoenix strip."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_H = "#ADD8E6"      # Light Blue
        COLOR_NOT_H = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Likelihoods describe how evidence appears under each scenario."
        # Visualizing the hypothesis spaces (priors)
        # Strip H: Represents prior probability of Phoenix existence
        strip_h = Rectangle(width=1.0, height=4.0, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        self.place_in_area(strip_h, 'B2', 'E2')
        
        # Strip not H: Represents prior probability of Phoenix non-existence
        strip_not_h = Rectangle(width=3.0, height=4.0, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        self.place_in_area(strip_not_h, 'B3', 'E5')
        
        label_h = Text("Phoenix (H)", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        label_not_h = Text("No Phoenix (not H)", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        
        # Position labels above strips
        label_h.next_to(strip_h, UP, buff=0.2)
        label_not_h.next_to(strip_not_h, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(
            Create(strip_h),
            Create(strip_not_h),
            Write(label_h),
            Write(label_not_h),
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "If the Phoenix is present, finding a feather is likely."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_H),
            strip_h.animate.set_stroke(COLOR_H, width=4)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "We shade a tall region within the Phoenix strip."
        # Likelihood P(E|H) = 0.9 -> Height 3.6 of 4.0
        fill_h = Rectangle(
            width=1.0, 
            height=3.6, 
            fill_color=COLOR_H, 
            fill_opacity=0.6,

        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_H),
            FadeIn(fill_h, shift=UP),
            Write(label_p_eh)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "If absent, finding a feather is just a fluke."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_NOT_H),
            strip_not_h.animate.set_stroke(COLOR_NOT_H, width=4)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "We shade a tiny region in the non-Phoenix strip."
        # Likelihood P(E|not H) = 0.05 -> Height 0.2 of 4.0

section_1.title: The Detective's Dilemma: Introducing Prior Belief
section_1.content: Introduce the core concept of Bayes' Theorem not as a dry formula, but as a method for updating beliefs based on evidence. We start with a 'Prior Probability'—our best guess before seeing new data.
section_1.example: A Forest Ranger finds a rare 'Cerulean Feather'. She wonders: Is the legendary Blue Phoenix nearby? Without the feather, she knows the Phoenix is rare (1% chance). This 1% is her 'Prior Belief' (P(H)).

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Unit Square as the Universal Set
section_2.content: To visualize probability geometrically, we represent the entire 'Universe of Possibilities' as a 1x1 square with an area of 1. Any event is a sub-area within this square.
section_2.example: Draw a square. Split it vertically: a thin sliver (1%) represents 'Phoenix is Present' (H), and the remaining 99% represents 'Phoenix is Absent' (¬H). The total area is 1.0.

section_3.title: The Evidence Filter (Likelihoods)
section_3.content: Introduce 'Likelihoods' as horizontal segments within our vertical strips. We ask: 'If the hypothesis were true, how likely is this evidence?' and 'If it were false, how likely is it?'
section_3.example: Within the 'Phoenix' strip, color 90% of the height to represent 'Likelihood of finding a feather if Phoenix exists' (P(E|H)). In the 'No Phoenix' strip, color a tiny 5% height for 'finding a feather by fluke' (P(E|¬H)).

section_4.title: The Geometry of the Intersection
section_4.content: Focus on the physical overlap. The 'Evidence' (E) has occurred, so everything outside the shaded 'Evidence' area is now impossible. We highlight the intersection of 'Hypothesis' and 'Evidence'.
section_4.example: The screen fades out the unshaded areas. We are left with two rectangles: A (Phoenix + Feather) and B (No Phoenix + Feather). The total area of these two rectangles is the 'Total Probability of Evidence' P(E).

section_5.title: Updating the Belief: The Posterior
section_5.content: Explain that the new probability is simply the ratio of the 'Success' rectangle to the 'Total Evidence' area. This is 'Normalizing' our world to the new evidence.
section_5.example: Zoom into the rectangles from Section 4. The updated belief (Posterior) is: Area(Phoenix + Feather) divided by [Area(Phoenix + Feather) + Area(Fluke Feather)]. Geometrically, it's the proportion of the 'Evidence Strip' that belongs to our Hypothesis.

section_6.title: Mapping Geometry to the Formula
section_6.content: Overlay the standard mathematical notation of Bayes' Theorem onto the geometric shapes created in the previous steps to solidify the connection.
section_6.example: Show P(H|E) = [P(H) * P(E|H)] / P(E). The numerator is the Area of the 'Target Rectangle'; the denominator is the 'Total Shaded Area'. Use color-coded labels to link the variables to the square's dimensions.

import numpy as np

        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
